task.title: Robot and the Lost Cat
task.prompt: A small delivery robot searches for a lost kitten on a rainy neon night.

style_guide.name: Robot and the Lost Cat Style Guide
style_guide.visual_style: warm cinematic comic illustration with clean linework, soft shading, and expressive panels
style_guide.typography: legible post-processed comic lettering, clear speech bubbles, simple uppercase captions
style_guide.negative_prompt: photorealistic horror, gore, grotesque faces, muddy anatomy, blurred text, cluttered panels

revision_lessons: Round 1: [medium] asset_consistency - Retry panel with stricter prompt emphasis on minimal readable signage and only one intentional text element: the speech bubble.
Round 1: [high] visual_defect - Retry panel 2 with explicit instruction to avoid any panel numbering, posters with readable text, or incidental typography inside the artwork.
Round 1: [medium] story_coherence - Simplify the scene so the pawprints and robot gesture dominate the composition.
Round 1: [high] asset_consistency - Retry panel 3 using the character reference more strictly, with the kitten kept tiny, simplified, and visually matched to the rest of the comic.
Round 1: [high] visual_defect - Regenerate panel 3 with explicit suppression of all incidental readable text except the speech bubble.
Round 1: [high] task_fit - Retry panel 4 with only the dialogue bubble retained and all other readable text removed from the image area.
Round 1: [high] asset_consistency - Regenerate panel 4 with stronger adherence to the character reference sheet and simplified kitten features.
Round 1: [medium] story_coherence - Use cleaner staging focused on robot and kitten interaction, with background text minimized or removed.
Round 1: [high] visual_defect - Redo page composition so each panel image fills its panel frame appropriately, with consistent cropping and minimal dead space.

Round 1: [high] text_layout_quality - Use either in-panel speech bubbles or external caption/dialogue boxes, not both. Prefer removing the bottom text boxes if speech bubbles are already rendered in the art.
Round 1: [medium] task_fit - Increase title hierarchy or remove it; prioritize stronger panel integration, balanced margins, and consistent comic-page typography.

planned_assets.title: Main Character Reference
planned_assets.description: A consistent reference sheet for the delivery robot and lost kitten to ensure visual continuity across all panels.
planned_assets.prompt: Warm cinematic comic illustration with clean linework, soft shading, and expressive character modeling. Create a clean character reference sheet for a story about a small delivery robot and a tiny lost kitten. Show the robot and kitten with consistent proportions, clear silhouette, and distinctive details that can be reproduced across panels: the robot is compact, friendly, and slightly rounded with visible delivery compartment accents; the kitten is very small, cute, and simple in shape with a recognizable face and tail. Present front, side, and 3/4 views or equivalent reference poses on a neutral or subtly tinted background. Use the palette amber, cobalt blue, and rainy gray with gentle, hopeful, slightly mysterious mood. Add simple labeled callouts if needed, with legible English text only. Avoid photorealistic horror, gore, grotesque faces, muddy anatomy, blurred text, and cluttered layout.

planned_assets.title: Panel 1: Opening
planned_assets.description: Establish the rainy neon city setting and the robot noticing the kitten is missing.
planned_assets.purpose: Tell one beat of the comic narrative.
planned_assets.prompt: Warm cinematic comic illustration with clean linework, soft shading, expressive faces, and strong readable composition. Comic panel 1 of 4 for 'Robot and the Lost Cat'. Establish a rainy neon city at night with wet pavement, glowing signage reflections, and cobalt-blue shadows. Show a small delivery robot in the foreground scanning the street with a concerned but determined posture, realizing the kitten is missing. Make the setting vivid and atmospheric, with amber highlights and rainy gray tones, while keeping the panel uncluttered and easy to read. Include one clear speech bubble in legible English: 'Where did the kitten go?' Avoid photorealistic horror, gore, grotesque faces, muddy anatomy, blurred text, and cluttered panels.
